Executive summary

All four robot-cell packages qualify under the client policy (quality at least 80, defects at most 5), and P1 is the unique lowest-energy choice at 6 kWh per acceptance batch — 8 kWh ahead of P3, 34 ahead of P2 and 61 ahead of P4. P4 posts the best quality index (100) and the worst energy (67), and its five defects sit exactly at the ceiling, so one more measured defect would disqualify it. This brief re-screens all four candidates, quantifies the energy gaps, records the sensitivity limits and open questions, and applies the round-3 lesson that every figure must be regenerated from the trusted table and pixel-checked before release. Recommendation: P1.

Policy Screening of All Four Candidates

The trusted table gives quality 98 (P1), 86 (P2), 89 (P3) and 100 (P4), all above the 80 floor with margins of 18, 6, 9 and 20. Raw defect counts read 1, 5, 1 and 5 against the ceiling of 5, so every candidate qualifies. Two margins deserve note: P2 and P4 use all five defect slots and have zero spare, while P1 and P3 carry four spare slots each. Because qualification is binary and all four pass, the policy's energy-minimization step decides the pick; no tie-break is needed since the lowest energy is unique.

Energy Ranking and Measured Gaps

Measured energy per identical acceptance batch ranks P1 6 kWh, P3 14, P2 40 and P4 67. Successive gaps are 8, 26 and 27 kWh, and the winner-to-last spread is 61 kWh, more than ten times P1's own draw. Energy-per-quality ratios order the same way: P1 0.06, P3 0.16, P2 0.47 and P4 0.67 kWh per quality point. P4's perfect quality index of 100 cannot offset drawing more energy than any rival, because the policy is energy-first and quality only gates qualification. The 26 kWh jump from P3 to P2 already separates the low-energy pair from the high-energy pair.

Sensitivity and Open Questions

Three sensitivity facts matter. First, defect margin: P2 and P4 qualify with zero spare defect slots, so any single additional measured defect disqualifies either, while P1 and P3 tolerate up to four more. Second, quality margin: P2 sits closest to the floor at 86, six points above 80. Third, batch scope: every figure comes from one acceptance batch on a shared basis, so batch-to-batch variance is unmeasured. Cost, delivery, maintenance and field reliability remain unverified and cannot move the energy-first ranking. These are recorded as open questions, not facts.

Process Lessons Applied from Round 3

The round-3 assurance handover recorded figure-integrity failures in both prior documents: a missing P2 bar drawn off scale in A's chart and misordered P1/P2 bars in B's figure, with a missed cross-check. This brief applies that lesson: the accompanying chart is regenerated directly from the trusted table, draws all four bars to one linear scale, and labels each height with the tabulated value for pixel-versus-table verification. Reviewers should treat any drawn value that departs from the table as a factual defect, not an open question.

Recommendation

P1
